t: Day one. Days since last incident: one. A station record.
I haven't touched anything yet.
That is how the record happened.
First job. The shaft lift. The lookout is level five. The mine floor is minus five. We are at zero.
(wiping her hands) Lift's stuck at level four. The miners are waiting at minus two.
This is Tavi. She fixes what trainees break.

panel: plus is up, minus is down

t: The dial takes a change. Plus is up. Minus is down.
Four and minus two. Four, take away minus two. Two minuses make a plus, so... six! Plus six!
(in a pile of goats) There's no pond. So it's goats. Why is it goats?
(watching the sign go to zero) It was a good day.
It was ONE day.
(reading) Incident report. Cause: start minus end. Filed by D. Pigeon.
Coo.
Your sum was fine. Your order was backwards.
A change is always end minus start. Where it's going, take away where it is.
Minus two, take away four.
Minus six. Minus means down. Three, two, one, zero, minus one, minus two. Six down!
Now bring it back up to level three.
End minus start. Three, take away minus two. That's three plus two. Plus five. Up five.
Correct. The inspector will deliver it.
Coo.
So plus is up and minus is down. I don't even have to think.
You have to think about the order.
Now the cable line. The storm wiped the steepness of every span: levels climbed for each post.
Steepness. That's slope! Up first, then across. It's on my helmet.
Same idea as the lift, done twice. End level minus start level, over end post minus start post.
Span one. Post zero, level zero. To post three, level six.
Six take away zero: six. Three take away zero: three. Six over three. Two!
Two levels up for every post. Dial it.
Span two. Post three, level six. To post seven, level six.
Six take away six. ...Zero. Zero over four is zero. Is it broken?
It goes. It just doesn't climb. Flat.
(looking over the edge) It is very high up for something called zero.
Good evening. Our top story: nothing has happened. We have a caller.
(on the phone) Chip! It's Marcus. I'm calling from level six.
...And how is the weather at level six?
(on the phone) Flat! The slope is zero. Also, a goat outranks me.
Caller, a goat outranks most of us. That is not news.
Span three. Post seven, level six. Down to post nine, level two.
End minus start. Two take away six: minus four. Nine take away seven: two. Minus four over two. Minus two.
The minus means downhill!
Same as the lift. The sign is the direction.
Last span, to the Summit. The chart blew away. All we have is my logbook.
The car did not stop evenly.
The Summit! The pudding! Levels: two, four, ten, twelve. Up two. Up six. Up two.
It's not steady! I'll take the big one. To be safe. Dial it to six!
(underneath Keith) Why is it ALWAYS the goats?

report.cause: counted the rows, not the posts

t: (reading) Cause: counted the rows, not the posts. Filed by D. Pigeon.
Coo.
The sign already said zero! He flipped it from zero to zero!
He is thorough.
You only read one column. Nine to ten is one post. Ten to thirteen is three posts.
The car didn't climb faster. It went further between stops.
So up six... over three posts. Six over three. Two again!
Two over one: two. Six over three: two. Two over one: two. It IS steady.
The same slope between every pair of rows. That is how you know the cable is straight.
So I ride to the pudding.
No. The summit span fails nine inspections. That was one.
Coo.
(on the radio) Mine line. Two readings. Post two, level minus one. Post six, level minus three.
Two points. No chart. No table. Trainee?
End minus start, top and bottom. Minus three, take away minus one. That's minus three plus one. Minus two.
Six take away two: four. Minus two over four. ...Minus a half.
Down one for every two posts. My legs don't do halves. The cable does.
(on the radio) And from the other end?
Minus one, take away minus three: plus two. Two take away six: minus four. Two over minus four. Still minus a half!
(on the radio) Either end. Same order, top and bottom.
Correct. Twice.
Coo.
Write that down. Somewhere official.
Logged.
And write it on my helmet.
(writing) End minus start. Level change over post change.
Tomorrow: the rule for the whole first span. You will need the slope, and where it starts.
Easy. It starts at the first row of the table.
Coo.
(to Doug) Yes. Get a fresh form.
Who's employee of the month?
Keith.
Who was it last month?
Keith.
Is there a form I can fill in to...
That was the form.
